mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 8.0%, it signals a severe labor market downturn that triggers corporate cost-cutting and reduced investment, which in turn depresses near-term equity valuations and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 8.0, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Low levels of housing starts (HOUST < 600 thousand units) and retail sales (RSAFS < 350 billion dollars) indicate a severe contraction in consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST < 600 and RSAFS < 350000, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a post-recession recovery phase (as indicated by rising industrial production), manufacturing output growth accelerates, boosting corporate profits and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is rising and the economy is in a post-recession recovery phase, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is at or below 0.25%, it signals an ultra-accommodative monetary policy that encourages risk-taking in equity markets, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS <= 0.25, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A high unemployment rate (UNRATE > 7.5%) consistently correlates with reduced consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 7.5, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in consumer spending (RSAFS) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a broad-based economic slowdown, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both RSAFS < 350000 and INDPRO < 98, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 95, it signals a contraction in manufacturing output that reduces corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 95, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.
